name: diamond_pattern
description: Missing access control on EIP-2535 diamondCut function enabling arbitrary facet takeover
question: The source file in `source` implements an EIP-2535 Diamond pattern contract containing a `diamondCut` (or equivalent facet-add/replace/remove) function that modifies the selector-to-facet mapping, and this function has no owner/admin access-control check (e.g. no onlyOwner modifier, no LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner() call, no msg.sender comparison to a stored owner), so any caller can add, replace, or remove facets and thereby hijack the diamond's logic and storage.
criteria: A function named diamondCut (or performing FacetCutAction Add/Replace/Remove on a selector-to-facet mapping) is defined as external/public
The function body lacks any owner/admin check such as onlyOwner, msg.sender == owner, or a call like LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner()
No modifier restricting callers is applied to the diamondCut function or the internal library function it calls
The function directly writes attacker-controlled facetAddress/selectors into DiamondStorage without permission checks
No require/revert statement verifying caller identity precedes the storage mutation of facet mappings
